A recall has been issued for certain lots of chlorthalidone, a medication commonly used to treat high blood pressure. (Getty Images) Check your medicine cabinet if you take blood pressure medication. Inventia Healthcare Limited issued a voluntary recall of certain bottles of chlorthalidone tablets, a common blood pressure drug, the Food and Drug Administration announced . The recall, initiated on June 5, covers 11,460 bottles — sold in 100-tablet and 1,000-tablet sizes — from two specific batches (RISA24001 and RISB24002), both with an expiration date of April 2027. The bottles were distributed nationwide by Rising Pharma Holdings of East Brunswick, N.J. The reason for this voluntary recall is "Failed Dissolution Specifications," according to the FDA, meaning the prescription medication may not dissolve properly, which can impact how the drug is released and absorbed by the body. High blood pressure is common — and often requires medication Around 50% of U.S. adults have hypertension, meaning they have high blood pressure, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . Blood vessels function like pipes , and the more pressure they face, the more damage they sustain over time. This causes them to stiffen and narrow, making it harder for oxygen-rich blood to reach organs like the heart and brain. As a result, people with high blood pressure face a higher risk of developing serious conditions like heart disease and stroke.
